issues.description: The `_enable_vad` invariant is stated by code but not by comment, and its semantics now diverge from its name.
issues.detail: `_enable_vad` is now False for both FIXED and EXTERNAL modes, meaning 'VAD events are emitted from this plugin'. The name suggests 'VAD is enabled.' A literate one-line comment stating the invariant ('True iff this plugin emits VAD/interruption frames; false when Pipecat or fixed-turn drives endpointing') would prevent the next reader from inverting the predicate.

issues.description: Default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silent behavioral break with no migration note in the docstring.
issues.detail: The docstring is updated, but existing users relying on EXTERNAL as default will silently get FIXED on upgrade, changing endpointing semantics. A literate comment or changelog line stating 'previous default was EXTERNAL; set explicitly to retain old behavior' is the kind of explanation a serious reader expects. Tests do not cover the default-switch case.

issues.description: Membership test uses a list literal where a frozenset or tuple is idiomatic and faster.
issues.detail: `self._config.end_of_utterance_mode not in [EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED, EndOfUtteranceMode.EXTERNAL]` allocates a list each construction. Not hot, so this is squarely premature-optimization territory to fix — but a tuple literal is the same characters and conventionally signals 'constant set.' Leave alone if style guide is silent.

issues.description: Frame-handler swap from `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` to `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` lacks a stated rationale comment.
issues.detail: The change is correct under the new model (VAD-specific frame triggers finalize only when external VAD is the source of truth), but the reader has to infer this from the frame name. One sentence — 'finalization is driven by VAD-origin stop frames so that fixed-turn/external modes don't double-finalize' — would make the handler self-explanatory.

issues.description: Commented-out `start_processing_metrics()` call moved but not deleted; intent is unclear.
issues.detail: The line `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` migrated from after the interruption frame to before it. If it is dead code, delete it; if it is a deliberate placeholder for a future ordering decision, a one-line TODO with the reason is the literate version. Drifting commented code accumulates as noise.

issues.description: `split_sentences` is forwarded by the generic loop and then overwritten by a dedicated assignment.
issues.detail: `split_sentences` is listed in the keys loop and then `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)` is set unconditionally below. Either remove it from the keys list (it is not a flat config field) or drop the dedicated assignment. The current code does both, which is the kind of double-write that confuses careful readers.

review.summary: The diff is small and behaviorally clear: finalize on VAD-specific stop frames, default to FIXED turn detection, and add a `split_sentences` passthrough. Algorithmically nothing changes — no loops, no new data structures, no complexity claims to audit. The substantive risks are not in the algorithm but in the literate-programming layer: the `_enable_vad` predicate's invariant is unstated and its name now mismatches its semantics, the default-mode flip is a silent migration with no in-source explanation, and `split_sentences` is written through two paths. UNDER-AUDITED on the comment/invariant axis; RIGOROUS enough on the mechanics.
